guard: The history limits of CHAT, INBOX, DLV and DM: a new space starts with no age limit and 1000 per sender, 1000 per agent lifecycle and no count, `cotal up` and an open-mode connect leave every existing stream's limit as it is and setup still refuses one of them that is not canonical apart from its limit, the provisioner may update those four streams and no other message stream, a broker refusal of the update is not reported as an unknown outcome, the setter keeps each stream's own bounds, the stored-copies notice follows the count stamped on each copy with an unstamped copy counting as 1000, recall reads the stream's own limits and its head, and durable catch-up copies what the stream holds without judging retention.
why: The suite imports core from `src`, so no build is needed and each mutant is what the suite runs. Every cell
runs against a live broker, so a mutation is graded by the broker's own permission checks, expiry and stored
config, and the stamp cells by real copies the delivery daemon's writer stored. Each mutation reddens a different named cell.

mutations.replace: const streamReconcile = [...ttlStreams, `KV_${membershipBucket(space)}`, OBJ, INBOX, DLV, DM]

mutations.cell: the provisioner may set the chat stream's limit
mutations.note: Without the grant `cotal history limit` is refused on every authed space.

mutations.cell: a new space's chat stream starts with no age limit and 1000 per sender

mutations.cell: its DM stream starts with no age limit and no count limit

mutations.name: cotal up moves a stream on the old settings to 30 days, as 0.134.0 did
mutations.find: for (const stream of ["chat", "inbox", "dlv", "dm"] as const) await readHistoryStreamConfig(jsm, opts.space, stream);
mutations.replace:
for (const stream of ["chat", "inbox", "dlv", "dm"] as const) await readHistoryStreamConfig(jsm, opts.space, stream);
    { const { config } = await jsm.streams.info(chatStream(opts.space)); if (config.max_age === 0 && config.max_msgs_per_subject === 1000) await setHistoryLimit(jsm, opts.space, "chat", { maxAgeMs: 30 * 86_400_000, perSubject: 1000 }); }
mutations.expectRed: cotal up leaves a chat stream with no age and 1000 per sender (every chat stream's limit before 0.134.0) as it is
mutations.cell: cotal up leaves a chat stream with no age and 1000 per sender (every chat stream's limit before 0.134.0) as it is
mutations.note: The move deleted every post older than 30 days at an ordinary upgrade (#5643).

mutations.replace: for (const stream of ["chat"] as const) await readHistoryStreamConfig(jsm, opts.space, stream);

mutations.cell: an INBOX stream with any setting other than its limit off canonical is refused, and left as it was
mutations.note: `createSpaceStreams` skips an existing INBOX, DLV or DM stream, so this read is the only check of one at `cotal up`.

mutations.cell: setHistoryLimit refuses an age below the two-hour duplicate window on inbox

mutations.cell: setHistoryLimit accepts no age and no count on chat

mutations.cell: copies stored under 5 still warn, at 5, after the count is raised to 50

mutations.find: if (limit !== null && m.info.pending >= limit - 1) this.emit("stored-copies-full", { limit });
mutations.replace: if (limit !== null && m.info.pending >= limit) this.emit("stored-copies-full", { limit });

mutations.cell: copies stored under 5 still warn, at 5, after the count is raised to none

mutations.name: the writer stops stamping its count
mutations.expectRed: copies stored under 5 still warn, at 5, after the count is raised to 50
mutations.cell: copies stored under 5 still warn, at 5, after the count is raised to 50
mutations.note: An unstamped copy counts as 1000, so a store full at 5 says nothing.

mutations.name: the writer never reads the count again
mutations.expectRed: copies stored under no count give no notice after the count drops to 5
mutations.cell: copies stored under no count give no notice after the count drops to 5
mutations.note: The writer's first stored copy in the suite is under 5, so a writer that keeps that read stamps 5 on copies stored under no count.

mutations.name: an unstamped copy counts as no count
mutations.expectRed: 1000 copies without the stamp warn, at 1000, as the old daemon's count was
mutations.cell: 1000 copies without the stamp warn, at 1000, as the old daemon's count was
mutations.note: A copy without the stamp comes from a daemon whose count was always 1000 (SPEC §8).

mutations.name: an unstamped copy counts as 999
mutations.expectRed: 999 copies without the stamp give no notice
mutations.cell: 999 copies without the stamp give no notice

mutations.name: catch-up judges the per-sender count again
mutations.find: await this.catchupCopy(owner, lifecycleUid, channel, joinCursor, fence, generation);
mutations.replace:
await this.catchupCopy(owner, lifecycleUid, channel, joinCursor, fence, generation);
    { const info = await this.jsm!.streams.info(chatStream(this.space), { subjects_filter: chatSubject(this.space, "*", "*", channel) }); if (Object.values(info.state.subjects ?? {}).some((n) => n >= info.config.max_msgs_per_subject)) { await tombstoneMember(kv, channel, owner, lifecycleUid, fence, this.card.id, generation); return { durable: false, reason: "activation catch-up window partially evicted by retention", generation }; } }
mutations.expectRed: a join whose channel is exactly at the per-sender count, behind another channel's post, activates with both posts
mutations.cell: a join whose channel is exactly at the per-sender count, behind another channel's post, activates with both posts
mutations.note: Stream state cannot tell this channel's eviction from another channel's removal, so a sender at the count proves nothing; the mutant tombstones a join that lost nothing.

mutations.cell: recall reports a channel whose posts are all gone, with the stream head past the watermark

mutations.name: recall judges the count against the compiled 1000, not the stream's limit
mutations.expectRed: recall reports a channel where a sender passed the stream's per-sender count
mutations.cell: recall reports a channel where a sender passed the stream's per-sender count
